speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To start, how old is the child and when did you first notice the bleeding and petechiae? Have there been any recent illnesses, fevers, or new medications introduced?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the combination of epistaxis, gum bleeding, bruising, and petechiae in a 4-year-old is concerning. Has the child had any recent fevers, infections, or been diagnosed with a viral illness in the past few weeks? Also, are there any family history of bleeding disorders?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see the bleeding symptoms are persistent; have you noticed any fever, bone pain, or unusual fatigue in the child recently? Also, does the child have a history of easy bruising or bleeding that started before age two?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical issues. Up-to-date on vaccinations. Social history: Attends preschool. Lives with parents and one older sibling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child experienced any fever, night sweats, or bone pain recently, and are there any enlarged lymph nodes or a swollen liver/spleen you've noticed? I will also need to order some blood work to check his platelet count and blood smear. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Temperature: 36.8°C (98.2°F) - No fever noted. Complete Blood Count: WBC 6,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.1 g/dL, Platelets 280,000 /μL (normal). Peripheral Blood Smear: No clumping of platelets observed, normal morphology of other cells. Coagulation Profile: PT 12 seconds (normal), aPTT 30 seconds (normal). Special Test (ELISA Binding Assay): Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors. Physical Exam Findings: Diffuse petechiae on forearms, legs, and trunk; mild gum bleeding on probing; dried blood at nares. No significant lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly noted in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count and coagulation profile, combined with the specific ELISA result showing a deficiency in GIIb/IIIa receptors, points directly to a congenital defect in platelet function rather than a count issue. This clinical picture is classic for Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann's Thrombasthenia.
